messages:
Priya: quick heads-up — we've got a repro for weird partial-JSON in streaming responses hitting both the Swift and Rust SDKs. It shows up when large batches + emojis are returned.
Alex: can you paste a small raw chunk capture? is auth refresh in the middle?
Priya: pasted below (sanitized). note the chunk boundary splits a multibyte emoji and leaves a trailing `,` in the partial object. auth tokens look stable, we see a reconnect around the same time though.
Priya: ```
...
{"id":1,"text":"hello \ud83d"
{"id":2,"text":"world"}
...
```
Jamal: yep that's classic UTF-8 split. Some clients treat each chunk as a separate ndjson line and fail to reassemble. Swift's String(decoding:as:) will throw if bytes invalid.
Sara: on the Rust side we switched to serde_json::StreamDeserializer and a small byte buffer to hold incomplete frames. that helped but we still saw stalls when the reader couldn't keep up (backpressure).
Mika: are we seeing TCP-level pause or just the parsing backlog? any socket read backlog metrics?
Priya: socket read queue looks fine. The runtime's streaming window gets saturated because we batch many requests and then the client-side parser blocks GC/processing for ~50-200ms under load.
Alex: hmm. two angles: 1) make parsers incremental/nonblocking (streaming decoder + small ring buffer), 2) add explicit flow-control between server and SDK — e.g., limit concurrent in-flight SSE events or send lightweight heartbeats to keep consumers progressing.
Sara: implemented StreamDeserializer + peek-and-accumulate; we still had edge cases where the first byte of a multibyte sequence arrived at end of chunk and next chunk dropped a leading 0xEF. fixed by always concatenating remainder bytes to next read.
Mika: could we add an opt-in "sse_reassembly" flag in SDKs so we don't change default behavior and customers can enable safe mode?
Priya: yes, let's do opt-in. also want a small runtime change: if parser backlog > N ms, emit a flow-control header to server to reduce server batching temporarily. that buys breathing room.
Alex: for Swift, recommend using Data and `withUnsafeBytes` to append remainder slice cheaply. send a tiny PR that shows the pattern. for Rust, serde_json::de::IoRead + StreamDeserializer works but need to guard against OOM by bounding buffer length.
Jamal: added a minimal patch in an internal branch to cap buffered bytes at 64KB and drop with a metric if exceeded (configurable). we should surface that metric to Console.
DevEx Bot: CI run for "devex/sse-reassembly" finished: 28 tests passed, 2 flaky streaming tests. see https://ci.internal/reports/1234
Mika: follow-ups: (1) Priya/ Sara: draft SDK opt-in flag design, (2) Jamal: add metric + alert for buffered-bytes, (3) Alex: sample Swift snippet for docs, (4) I'll file an infra ticket to allow transient flow-control headers.
Priya: I'll open the SDK PRs today, include small repro harness and a note about emoji/multibyte boundary in tests. linking once ready. thanks all :rocket:
Alex: cheers — ping me for code review when you're ready.
Sara: will add the Rust example and a unit test that simulates 1-byte splits.
Jamal: will wire the metric to a dashboard and add an Ops playbook note.
Mika: leaving this open for updates. marked as FYI in #eng-runtime.
Priya: thanks — closing for now, will update thread when PRs are up.
